q: Which single sign, phase, or Pauli-frame convention in Eqs. (3)-(5) of Hen 2014, when corrected, brings the adiabatic Hadamard block to unit fidelity against the textbook Hadamard on all single-qubit inputs?
basis: We tested 4 obvious sign variants (flipping the sigma_x or sigma_y term, swapping the |+-y> subspace assignments); none reached >0.6 mean fidelity across 5 random random-input states at N=2000 slices and T=20. The as-printed Hamiltonian gives Trotter-converged fidelity 0.049..0.522 and the aux qubit consistently P(|1>)=0.9946 (not 1.0), all pointing at a real Hamiltonian mismatch, not a numerics issue.
next_steps: Run an 8-way parity sweep over all combinations of {sign(sigma_x), sign(sigma_y), sign(sigma_z), subspace-swap, global i-phase on the |-y> sub-branch}, plus an analytic re-derivation of the paper's Eq. (7) starting from the sign-variant Hamiltonian and checking which reduces to Eq. (8). Contact the author (itayhen@isi.edu) with the variant that resolves it.

q: For the CP-shift and CNOT blocks we get P(aux=|1>) = 0.999973 at N=3000 slices, not exactly 1. Is this residual pure Trotter-slice error (which scales as dt^2 for midpoint rule), or a residual non-adiabatic transition that survives dt -> 0 at finite T?
basis: The observed defect 1 - 0.999973 = 2.7e-5 is order-of-magnitude compatible with dt^2 = (25/3000)^2 = 6.9e-5, so probably discretization. But we did not decouple dt from T in the sweep.
next_steps: Fix T=25 and sweep N in {1000,2000,4000,8000,16000} (dt halves each time); fit log(1-fid) vs log(dt). Then fix N=8000 and sweep T in {5,10,25,50,100} (adiabaticity varies, dt varies); separate the two scaling laws. This will distinguish adiabatic error (Landau-Zener-like, exponentially small in T) from discretization error (algebraic in dt).

q: The paper warns that this construction sacrifices AQC's natural gap protection because the ground-state manifold is doubly degenerate. What is the smallest concrete open-system simulation that quantitatively demonstrates the crossover between 'adiabatic gate works' and 'adiabatic gate fails due to decoherence'?
basis: Our closed-system CP-shift and CNOT fidelities of 0.999973 give a clean baseline. The paper argues (Sec. 4) that dephasing in the energy eigenbasis is a specific vulnerability of the degenerate-ground-state construction relative to standard AQC. A quantitative benchmark is missing from the paper.
next_steps: Add Lindblad dissipators L_k = sqrt(gamma) sigma_z on each qubit (pure dephasing) or L_k = sqrt(gamma) sigma_- (amplitude damping), sweep gamma*T in {0, 1e-4, 1e-3, 1e-2, 1e-1, 1}, and measure the CP-shift gate fidelity floor. Compare with a traditional AQC benchmark (e.g., 3-qubit Ising ground-state prep) at the same gamma*T to quantify the 'lost robustness' the paper flags qualitatively.

q: The CP-shift and CNOT Hamiltonians as written are strictly 3-local. What is the smallest 2-local gadget (using only ZZ, XX, XZ, YZ two-body terms available on realistic quantum annealers) that reproduces the CP-shift adiabatic gate at >=99% fidelity, and how does its adiabatic runtime scale relative to the 3-local original?
basis: The paper (Sec. 4) explicitly says 'adiabatic gates based on three-local interactions are currently beyond any practical reach' and suggests gadgets as a remedy, but does not construct one or benchmark its runtime cost. Our verified 3-local baseline (fidelity 1.000000 at T=25) is the ideal reference against which any 2-local gadget can be quantitatively compared.
next_steps: Build a perturbative-gadget reduction (Jordan-Farhi or Oliveira-Terhal style) that maps the |1><1|-tgt=|1><1|-aux three-body term to auxiliary ZZ-couplings. Run the same fidelity benchmark on the 2-local version for T in {25, 100, 400, 1600}; extract the T vs fidelity floor scaling to characterize the runtime penalty.

q: In our end-to-end 3-qubit QFT composition we cheated: we assembled the paper's H+CP+CNOT recipe from *ideal* gates (justified because C2/C3 showed the adiabatic Hamiltonians equal the ideal gates). If we instead compose the *actual* adiabatic-evolution output states end-to-end through all 7 gates + SWAP, how much does the between-gates aux-reset step matter?
basis: Each adiabatic gate leaves the aux in |1> at P=0.999973 and the data at fidelity 1.0 conditional on aux=|1>. Composing 7 such gates naively predicts 0.999973^7 = 0.9998 for the full QFT if errors are uncorrelated, but the paper does not analyze this compound and does not specify the aux-reset mechanism between gates.
next_steps: Implement an explicit aux-reset unitary (X_aux conditional on aux=|1> measurement, or equivalent) between the 7 adiabatic gates of the QFT_3 circuit. Run the full circuit statevector end-to-end and measure QFT_3 fidelity vs the ideal QFT_3 matrix. Compare with the multiplicative prediction 0.999973^7 to detect any correlated-error inflation.
